target_customer: B2C startups, customer experience teams, sales teams and AI agent builders who want to message customers over iMessage
problem: Apple offers no public iMessage API for businesses, so teams that want blue bubble conversations at scale have to build around Apple hardware and accounts themselves.
business_model: usage and subscription API (published tiers of $25 per month shared line and $250 per month dedicated line), plus an outbound as a service offering
product_category: iMessage, SMS and FaceTime messaging infrastructure for AI agents

founders.name: Gary Gao
education: University of Pennsylvania, computer science and business
founders.background_notes: YC page says he spent the past year researching ML model architectures and designing neuromorphic chips; no employers named.

founders.name: Ian Fong
education: New York University, mathematics (current student per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has won 8 hackathons including MIT, Harvard, Penn and Princeton.

competitors.name: Sendblue
competitors.what: iMessage API provider built on real Apple hardware
competitors.traction_then: describes itself as the largest iMessage API provider, operating over five years (self-reported)

competitors.name: Linq
competitors.what: iMessage API for business, markets SOC 2 Type II
competitors.traction_then: described by a rival as about two years old; self-reported

competitors.name: Blooio
competitors.what: iMessage API with flat rate plans aimed at AI agents

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable iMessage delivery at scale depends on managing Apple devices and accounts with no official API, plus webhooks, fallback to SMS and RCS, and voice and video bridging; hard operationally but built by two students.

defensibility.rationale: At least three rivals already sold the same wedge, comparison pages list near identical features, and the access method is not exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying outcome found as of the May to August 2026 launch coverage.

market_need_then: Businesses want conversational messaging in the channel customers trust; AI agents increased demand for programmable messaging, and Apple has no public business iMessage API (per launch coverage in 2026).

branding.domain_note: Uses trychert.com rather than chert.com (prefix domain).

identity.logo: Chert wordmark with a small icon
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, friendly, practical; headline reads Build AI people can text, call, and FaceTime.

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN as Twilio for iMessage (May 2026) and a Product Hunt launch; aggregator coverage in several languages.

brand_strength.rationale: A short real word name with a clear Twilio for iMessage tagline helped the HN launch, but no mascot, merch or brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Chert is a two person Spring 2026 YC company that launched in May 2026 with a Twilio for iMessage pitch in an already crowded niche. It is too early for an outcome; the open risks are dependence on non official iMessage access, competitors with SOC 2 and longer track records, and the thin moat.
notes: Funding: two aggregators (FundedIQ, EveryDev) report about $500k pre-seed, one dated June 2026 and one April 2026 with conflicting batch labels; no primary source, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Company site claims backing from YC, Z Fellows, Betafund and OpenAI, which search could not confirm. An aggregator says Gary Gao previously co-founded Flux; not verified. Competitor source dates are 2026 comparison pages, near launch, mostly vendor marketing. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed rests on FundedIQ (June 2026) and another aggregator (April 2026); month left out because of the conflict. Betafund and Z Fellows backing is claimed only on the company site. Single database level evidence.
